consigna: One sustained spoken production of at least ten minutes: explain a situation you have reconstructed from evidence — what probably happened, how sure you are, and where you disagree with the official account. With a person or recorded alone. Notes are preparation; the delivery is spoken.
requisitos: A deduction chain from *must have* down to a dismissed possibility (week 27)
Disagreement aimed at the source, not the person (week 30)
A summary calibrated to a listener without your context (week 32)
One register ladder used deliberately: phrasal, Latinate, fixed collocation (week 31)
One idiom, well placed, and only one (week 28)
microtareas: *Mon (10 min).* Reread the corrections from weeks 26 to 33 and note the most frequent one.
*Wed (5 min).* Write three sentences carrying a deduction, a hedge and a register choice together.
*Fri (10 min).* Record the ten minutes. Then listen to the last minute: does the precision hold to the end?
autochequeo: Did stacking hedges make me sound evasive anywhere?
Was the deduction a chain or a list?
Did the register stay chosen rather than accidental?
promptCorreccion: This is a review of six skills at once: modal deduction, hedging, disagreement, audience-calibrated summarising, register laddering and idiom use. (1) For each, say whether it is present and whether it is done well. (2) Say which collapsed. (3) Give me one sentence carrying three of them. Correct nothing outside these six areas. ---
